details:
Overview

CultivAI is a mobile platform that helps small-scale farmers plan crop rotations using NASA data. Crop rotation helps restore and conserve soil health and can provide long-term financial benefits, although these gains often take time to appear and may compete with short-term income needs (Rosa & Borsoi, 2022). Even so, many farmers struggle to understand when to rotate crops, which crops to choose, and what benefits they can expect.

Family farms account for approximately 77% of Brazil's agricultural establishments, representing around 3.9 million farms, according to the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE, 2019). However, research shows that family farmers face several barriers to adopting specialized digital tools for agricultural production and crop planning. Limited digital literacy is one of the main challenges (Dibbern et al., 2025). Technical language, unfamiliar interfaces, and text-heavy platforms can also discourage adoption (Stroparo et al., 2026). Research further suggests that family farmers often rely on general-purpose applications, such as WhatsApp, for communication rather than specialized tools for recording and managing agricultural production (Stroparo et al., 2026).

This challenge extends beyond Brazil. Limited literacy and restricted access to mobile phones can also prevent smallholder farmers in other countries, such as India, from benefiting from agricultural innovations (J-PAL, n.d.).

CultivAI addresses these barriers through an intuitive interface inspired by the communication apps farmers are already familiar with. The platform begins with a simple registration process that collects essential information about the farm, including its location, soil characteristics, and current crops. By combining this information with environmental data from NASA POWER, CultivAI uses an AI-powered chatbot to help farmers explore personalized crop rotation strategies through clear, accessible conversations.

The chatbot supports audio interaction, allowing farmers to engage with the platform in a more accessible way. CultivAI also includes a frequently asked questions section and an interactive calendar that organizes crop rotation recommendations into clear, actionable steps. Together, these features help farmers understand their options, keep track of their agricultural planning, and visualize the potential long-term benefits of their decisions.

CultivAI's creative approach lies in transforming complex scientific data into a familiar, conversation-based experience. Rather than requiring farmers to interpret technical information or navigate complicated interfaces, the platform prioritizes accessibility, simplicity, and human-centered design.

The result is an accessible agricultural decision-support tool that helps family farmers make more informed decisions using real environmental data. By reducing digital barriers and making crop rotation planning easier to understand, CultivAI aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices, improve soil conservation, and support long-term productivity without overwhelming its users.

Tools and Methodology

Our development process followed a human-centered design approach, starting with desk research, benchmarking, and user persona development to understand the challenges faced by small-scale farmers.

We used FigJam to organize our research, map stakeholders, brainstorm ideas using the 6-3-5 method, and prioritize features through the MoSCoW framework. In Figma Design, we created wireframes and adapted a style guide from the Figma Community using Claude AI, aligning it with our visual identity.

For development, we used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the interface, the NASA POWER API to access environmental data, the Groq API to power the AI chatbot, and Supabase to manage the database.

Throughout the process, we prioritized accessibility, simplicity, technical feasibility, and familiar interactions to make agricultural planning more intuitive for farmers with limited digital literacy.
